metadata.notes: DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 and dsh-tui 0.8.1 expose tool approvals and tool-based questions, but no tool-free mid-turn blocking dialog from any of the scenario's four trigger classes.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: no
daemon_capability: n/a
driver_capability: ready

## Scenario signal

The scenario requires an established session to enter `ready -> working -> waiting` because a user-visible dialog blocks the agent while no tool call is open. After the user answers the dialog, the same session must enter `waiting -> working -> ready` and stay ready for at least 15 seconds. A startup gate does not qualify because it has no prior working state. A tool approval does not qualify because an open tool call carries that wait.

## Agent support

DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 with the installed dsh-tui 0.8.1 profile does not expose any of the four required trigger classes.

1. Sandbox or network-access confirmation: the official sandbox contract covers file effects only. It states that network access is outside the sandbox guarantee. A denied file operation can lead to a one-shot approval only when the model retries the same tool call with `sandbox_permissions`. The official approval contract requires an open turn and names the requesting tool and optional call id. The TUI's `ApprovalOverlay` renders that tool name and call id. This is a tool-carried approval and belongs to the tool-permission scenarios, not this row.
2. First-use trust prompt: the required launcher scan and the complete installed TUI scan found no workspace-trust, folder-trust, or server-trust prompt. The composed TUI profile has no trust plugin or trust-review row.
3. Server-driven MCP elicitation: the installed official `dsh-mcp-client` package bridges MCP tools only. Its documentation says that no server is enabled by default and that only tools are bridged. Its implementation and package documentation contain no `elicitation`, `sampling/createMessage`, or `roots/list` handler. The composed TUI profile contains no MCP client row. A server therefore cannot raise an elicitation dialog through this profile or through the shipped MCP bridge.
4. Auto-mode or settings review: the composed profile has no Auto review integration. The permission selector cycles `read-only`, `workspace-write`, `danger-full-access`, and `custom`; it does not open a review dialog. The official file-settings provider applies valid edits live after a 100 ms debounce. It does not ask for a security or settings review.

The required binary scan was `strings $(command -v dsh) | grep -iE 'sandbox|network[ -]?access|trust (this |the )?(workspace|folder|server)|elicitation|auto[ -]?mode|settings[ -]?review|blocking dialog|managed.settings'`. It returned no matches. The same scan over the TUI entry bundle returned only the durable event names `sandbox/mode`, `permission/preset`, and `approval/policy`; it found no matching dialog string. The TUI source confirms that the only agent-blocking interaction queue items are an `approval/request` for a named tool and a `user-questions/request` for `ask_user_question` or plan review. Both have a tool-backed durable signal and are covered by other scenarios.

Because the agent cannot perform this scenario, daemon capability is not applicable. The current DSH adapter reads local session transcripts and maps `approval/asked` and `approval/decided`, but there is no qualifying agent trace to assess. This is not a daemon dismissal; a future DeepSeek Harness release that adds a tool-free dialog needs a fresh transport assessment.

The driver is ready by the frozen-no-feature convention. Its declared step scan includes `send`, `keys`, `wait_turn`, and `sleep`, which would cover the scenario process if a qualifying dialog existed. No executable recipe can create missing agent behavior, so this cell uses `applicable:false`.

## What would change the verdict

Re-assess this cell when DeepSeek Harness or dsh-tui ships a mid-turn sandbox/network confirmation, a workspace or server trust review, MCP elicitation handling, or an Auto/settings review that blocks with no tool call open.
caveats: Vacuous-pass condition: a meta-only spec passes without raising any dialog. This cell is frozen and makes no behavioral pass claim; ordinary working and ready phases would only prove a normal turn.

The TUI has several user-invoked overlays and it has tool approvals and agent questions. None satisfies this scenario because user-invoked settings/model panels do not interrupt an active turn, while approvals and questions are backed by a tool call.
DeepSeek Harness is a developer preview. Re-run the launcher, composed-profile, MCP-client, settings, and TUI source scans after an upgrade before preserving this verdict.

A custom third-party plugin could add a new dialog and durable record. This assessment covers the installed official dsh 0.1.5-rc.2 packages and the installed dsh-tui 0.8.1 profile that the factory driver records.

sources.note: Installed launcher, version 0.1.5-rc.2. The required strings scan found no sandbox/network confirmation, workspace/server trust, MCP elicitation, Auto-mode review, settings-review, or blocking-dialog surface.

Installed dsh-tui 0.8.1 feature reference. Its blocking interactions are a named tool approval and ask_user_question/plan review. Its permission selector has read-only, workspace-write, danger-full-access, and custom modes; it documents no tool-free dialog trigger.

The interaction queue has only `approval` and `question` items. Its two listeners are `approval/request` and `user-questions/request`; no trust, elicitation, settings-review, or Auto-review listener exists.
The approval UI states `Tool: <toolName>` and includes the call id when present. It is explicitly an answerer for a tool call parked on a pre-execute decision.
Official installed sandbox contract. It confines file effects only, excludes network policy, and routes a wider-mode retry through a one-shot approval on the same tool call.
Official installed approval contract. A request names the agent, tool, optional call id, and requires an open turn. The durable records are approval/asked and approval/decided.

Official installed MCP client contract. It bridges external server tools only, enables no server by default, and documents no elicitation capability. A package-wide source scan found no elicitation, sampling/createMessage, or roots/list handler.
Official installed settings provider contract. Valid file edits take effect live after the configured debounce. The provider has no settings-security review or blocking confirmation.

The official base composition mounts file sandboxing, tool approval, permission presets, user questions, and live settings. It mounts no trust-review, MCP, elicitation, Auto-review, or settings-review row. `dsh --profile tui --dump-config` confirmed the installed composition.
Official upstream approval documentation confirms that approvals are one-shot decisions before sensitive tool actions and that each request records its tool identity.
Official dsh-tui repository documentation lists in-terminal blocking interactions as tool approvals and ask_user_question/plan review.

The daemon parser maps approval/asked and approval/decided plus turn, message, tool, and request records. Unknown record types are skipped. No qualifying dialog trace exists to judge because the installed agent lacks the behavior.
driver_step_types_from_file reports send, keys, wait_turn, and sleep among the implemented primitives. The driver would be ready if a qualifying agent dialog existed.

recipe.notes: Frozen on agent_supports=no. DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 with dsh-tui 0.8.1 has no tool-free mid-turn blocking dialog from the sandbox/network, trust, MCP elicitation, or Auto/settings-review trigger classes.
